html_body:
🚨 Urgent — SPXC halal-breach exit still overdue (flagged again)

This was already raised urgently in yesterday's report: the halal-compliance breach (Kranze Technology Solutions defense-electronics exposure) was logged 2026-08-25 — 14 days ago — and the standing rule says a breach means exit at the next market open, regardless of P&L. SPXC is still showing as an open position in portfolio.json, resting behind a passive $205 exit-limit with a $186.90 stop underneath, not an active market exit. Markets reopen today (Tuesday) at 9:30am ET / 4:30pm Kuwait — several hours after this report goes out.

Action: if this hasn't already been closed out, cancel the resting $205 limit at the open and exit at market/aggressive limit regardless of price. If it already filled since the last sync, disregard this and let portfolio-manager know so the record updates.

⚠️ Price feed unavailable today

Yahoo Finance (query1 + query2) and the stooq fallback were all network-blocked in this run's environment (egress errors, not missing-data errors) — no live prices for GOOG or SPXC. I cannot confirm how close either position is to its stop ($333.90 GOOG / $186.90 SPXC) or TP, or whether SPXC's exit already filled. Check IBKR directly today.

Reading jumped from 232.5% in June to 237–241% now — about 5–8 points in ~10 weeks, a fast move for this metric. Forward P/E at ~20x looks almost boring next to that, which tells you the market-cap-to-GDP extreme is concentrated in a handful of mega-caps, not broad-based multiple expansion.

Implication for you: this isn't a reason to force a new entry. Keep the GOOG/SPXC stops tight and verified — a market this stretched corrects fast when it turns.

Last comparable episodes: 2000 dot-com peak, 2021 post-COVID peak. Live search confirmed this reading (not the hardcoded fallback) — GuruFocus 237.4% (Sep 7), other trackers 240.8% (Sep 4).

📰 Position News — Sep 8, 2026

🔵 GOOG

FTC investigation into YouTube (account-suspension / disclosure practices) reportedly in final stages, with a lawsuit said to be in prep — adds to a UK £300M ($353M) Play Store settlement already on the books. Analyst targets are widely split ($360 to $430 range) on capex-vs-cloud-growth debate. ⚠️ WATCH: regulatory overhang building, not urgent, but tracks toward the "Regulatory Overhang and De-Risking Events" concept taught earlier.

🟠 SPXC

Fundamentally the news is strongly bullish: Q2 beat + raised FY26 EPS guidance (midpoint $8.40), HVAC/data-center-cooling backlog +59% YoY to $919M, and four analyst firms (Truist, Oppenheimer, Wolfe, BofA) carry targets from $235 to $295 — all well above both your $199.92 entry and the $205 exit-limit. None of that changes the call: the Detection & Measurement segment's Kranze defense-electronics exposure still trips the no-defense rule, so the exit stands. Worth naming the size of the opportunity cost you're accepting on principle, not reversing it.

📚 Today you learned

Buffett Indicator, Part 2 — trend velocity matters as much as the level

You've seen the level before: total market cap ÷ GDP, and above 190% is historically danger territory. What's new since June is the trend — 232.5% then, 237–241% now, roughly 5–8 points in about ten weeks. The level tells you where you are; the rate of change tells you how fast you got there, and that's the part institutions actually watch. A slow grind from 190% to 200% over two years is a different risk profile than the same move in ten weeks — the fast version usually means capital piling into a narrow set of names, not broad-based re-rating. Your own book sits right in that narrow set via GOOG. It doesn't change your stop logic, but it's a reason to keep the stop tight rather than widen it "because the thesis is still good."

Also today: Shiller CAPE ratio — same idea as the Buffett Indicator but denominated in 10-year inflation-adjusted earnings instead of GDP; it's flashing similarly stretched right now, a second data point pointing the same direction.
